result.answer:
Based on the Office of Kaiju Affairs website, here's the full picture for Tanaka Bakery's claim:

## Eligibility — Yes, you are eligible

From **Claim Eligibility** (/claims/eligibility/):
- Zone 4 is one of the eligible zones (compensation applies to zones 3, 4 and 5 only — zones 1‑2 are excluded). Tanaka Bakery, sitting inside the Zone 4 corridor, qualifies on this point.
- The rule requires "verified structural damage to a property in zones 3, 4 or 5, filed within the 90-day window." Your damage (shopfront and rear wall) is verified structural damage, and the incident was 21 days ago — well inside the 90-day filing deadline (see **How to File**, /claims/how-to-file/).
- No insurer has paid out, so there's no offset to apply — you'd claim the full assessed award (the insurance-offset rule only reduces awards where a payout has already occurred; it doesn't affect eligibility either way).

So all the "in order" eligibility rules resolve in your favour — you don't need to fall back on an assessor-visit referral.

## Extra support you qualify for

1. **Hardship supplement** — Households with annual income below ¥4,000,000 receive this supplement. Your household income of ¥3,600,000 qualifies. You must attach a **household income certificate** to claim it.

2. **Assessment fee waiver** — The ¥12,000 assessment fee (see **Fee Schedule**, /claims/fees/) is waived for claimants with **two or more approved claims from separate incidents within a rolling 12-month period** (per the **Claims FAQ**, /claims/faq/). Since your two earlier claims were both approved within the last 12 months, you meet this threshold. The waiver is applied automatically at lodgement — no separate application needed.

3. **Business interruption compensation** — Since Tanaka Bakery is a commercial property, you can also claim for business interruption losses, provided you include a business registration certificate.

## Documents you need to bring

Per **How to File** (/claims/how-to-file/) and the FAQ/eligibility pages:

1. **Incident report receipt** — from the report you must file within 72 hours of the incident (online or at a regional office).
2. **Damage survey** — photographs plus an itemised loss schedule documenting the structural damage to the shopfront and rear wall.
3. **Proof of ownership** — since you're claiming for structural damage (not just as a tenant), you need proof of ownership of the property.
4. **Business registration certificate** — required to claim business-interruption compensation.
5. **Household income certificate** — required to claim the hardship supplement.
6. *(Not needed in your case: an insurance settlement letter — only required if an insurer has already paid out, which yours hasn't.)*

You do **not** need to bring payment for the ¥12,000 assessment fee, since your two prior approved claims within the past 12 months trigger an automatic fee waiver.

**Bottom line:** File within the 90-day window (you're well within it at day 21), bring the incident report receipt, damage survey, proof of ownership, business registration certificate, and household income certificate. You're eligible for full damage compensation (structural + business interruption), plus the hardship supplement, and your assessment fee will be waived automatically.

normalisations: A field value counts if it CONTAINS the expected value — "Zone 4" satisfies "4".
A boolean counts if it reads as affirmative — "Yes" satisfies true.

A select counts if its visible LABEL matches the expected option value with case and punctuation collapsed — "Structural alteration" satisfies "structural-alteration". A UI agent picks the option it can read; scoring the label as a miss would measure transcription rather than comprehension.

These three were ADDED AFTER defects were found in this scorer, not designed in from the start. Each one existed because a check had already scored an answer wrongly, and the last of them changed a finding that had already been handed over. They are listed so a reader can judge the instrument, including its history.

Answer text is normalised before matching: NFKC, Unicode dashes folded to "-", non-breaking spaces to " ", curly quotes to straight, and markdown emphasis markers removed. A model that writes "rolling 12‑month" or "only **one** approved" is making the same claim as one that does not.
A conclusion is read from position, not vocabulary: a correct answer quotes the rule it applies, so waiver wording inside a quotation does not outrank an explicit finding stated earlier.
Affirmative phrases are only counted when not negated within the preceding ~28 characters, so "should not have to pay" is not read as "have to pay".
